title: Substitution with closed bodies
prompt:
Here is a toy term language with numbers, params, Add, and Call(body, args). Write subst(args, t): replace every Param(i) reachable from t with args[i].

  • A nested Call's body is closed: leave it exactly as it is.
  • Its args are not: substitute inside them.
  • If there is no i-th arg, leave Param(i) alone.

This is the 101 vs 102 bug from above, on a type small enough to see in one screen. Keep the given show function, because the tests print with it.
hints: Write one `match` case per class. `Num` has nothing to replace. `Param(i)` is the only place a replacement happens.

For `Param(i)`, check `i < len(args)` before indexing, because `args[4]` on a short list raises `IndexError`. Keep the `Param` when there's no such arg. `Add` rebuilds itself from both substituted sides.
For `Call(body, xs)`, substitute inside each arg in `xs` but return `body` exactly as it is. Its params belong to that inner call, not to you.
explain: Substitution only touches `Param` nodes, rebuilds `Add` from its substituted sides, and at a nested `Call` rewrites the args but keeps the body. That is the closed-body rule: the inner body's `Param(0)` refers to the inner call's own args, so walking into it would wire in the wrong values.
